$comment: The hub's own IR blaster add-on (issue #42, firmware_ir_blaster/): a new one gets the WiFi over Bluetooth, protected by the code on its label (Espressif provisioning, security 2); one already on the WiFi is found by mDNS and paired with the same code. Placed next to ONE device with an IR remote, it becomes that device; its buttons are taught afterwards on the device's remote screen. Format: wiki Device-Templates.
name: IR remote device
description: Anything with an infrared remote (LED strips, projectors, fans, audio), controlled through the hub's IR blaster placed next to it. You teach it the remote's buttons after adding it.

inputs.label: Blaster address
inputs.hint: The blaster's console shows it: type `status`, e.g. 192.168.1.143

inputs.label: Pairing code
inputs.hint: On the blaster's label, or type `pairing` in its console: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX (small letters are fine)

inputs.label: WiFi name
inputs.hint: The network the blaster joins (2.4 GHz). The hub's own network is filled in.

inputs.label: WiFi password
inputs.hint: Leave empty for an open network. Only sent to the blaster, not kept on the hub.

steps.text: Plug the new IR blaster in, within a few metres of the hub. It waits for setup over Bluetooth: new, or after holding its BOOT button for 5 seconds.

steps.hint: Setting up the blaster: WiFi over Bluetooth, then pairing. This takes up to a minute.

setup.label: Already on the WiFi: find it

steps.text: Plug the IR blaster in next to the device it will control, and make sure it's on the WiFi.
